item.title: Michigan father's free Halloween display draws 18,000 visitors, sparks dispute with city officials
item.description: Nate Taylor launched Dead Ends on Spruce, a Halloween experience dedicated to families seeking a safe and fun outing. The festive display, equipped with animatronics and eerie soundscapes, started after an ad for complimentary decorations. Despite legal hurdles imposed by city officials, Taylor persevered. Last October, the event delighted around 18,000 visitors and provided special sessions for children with special needs, emphasizing inclusivity in community celebrations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Lost Eloise portrait found in dumpster sells for $100,000 after decades in closet
item.description: In a fascinating twist of fate, Eloise's original portrait, crafted by Hilary Knight in 1956, mysteriously disappeared during a Junior League Ball in 1960. Rediscovered in a dumpster, it lay dormant in Knight's closet for years, only to be brought back to life at a 2017 exhibition at the New-York Historical Society. Its subsequent auction at Bonhams in 2018 for $100,000 underscores the unpredictable journey and enduring value of art. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Insurer denies heart procedure for 12-year-old with Kawasaki disease
item.description: Rowan Lowry, a 12-year-old boy, urgently needs a stent procedure to address complications stemming from Kawasaki disease. His family faces an insurance denial categorizing the procedure as medically unnecessary. Undeterred, they plan to seek treatment at Boston Children's Hospital, driven by their concern for Rowan's deteriorating health and the fear of open-heart surgery. Determined, they vow to advocate fiercely for their son's well-being despite the financial strain. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teen Builds Rural Stem Access: Ontario student launches Project RISE; initiative widens STEM opportunities
item.description: At just 17 years old, Amara Wilson-Zegil is on a mission to bridge the gap in STEM education for children in rural areas. With an impressive outreach to over 1,800 students through robotics initiatives and camps, she has launched Project RISE. This groundbreaking initiative aims to combat educational disparities by providing vital tech experiences, ensuring more youth in Northern Ontario can access quality STEM opportunities. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
